newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich urges F-16 sale suspension to Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich urges F-16 sale suspension to Indonesia.

text.p: House (of Representatives) Speaker Newt Gingrich on Thursday called for suspension of U.S. sales of F-16 jets to Indonesia pending investigation of contributions by wealthy Indonesians to President Clinton's re-election campaign.

Gingrich told reporters the sale should "absolutely" be postponed as should any other U.S. government activity with regard to Indonesia. Next year, he said, congressional hearings will be held to investigate the campaign contributions and the development of the Clinton administration's policy toward the regime of Indonesian Gen. Suharto.

The Georgia Republican said he would hold hearings next year on U.S. policy towards the Jakarta government and the role of these campaign donations in development of that policy. However, this presumes his party retains control of Congress after the November elections, a situation that analysts now say is a toss-up.
"There's no question in my mind that we should postpone any actions towards Indonesia until we've had a chance to review this," he said.
The Clinton administration has said the Jakarta government did not receive favorable treatment.
"Contrary to whatever the innuendo is, we moved very aggressively toward Indonesia and have had a very tough policy toward them in many areas," a senior official told Reuters Wednesday.
Gingrich condemned the Clinton re-election campaign for reportedly accepting contributions of $425,000 from an Indonesian couple and $225,000 from a South Korean company.
